A judge orders the ex-OpenAI staffer charged with bugging an exec conference room released on $1M bond, finding prosecutors lack evidence to keep him in custody (Bloomberg)
A US jury finds Huawei guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud but acquits it of the most severe charge of criminal racketeering conspiracy (Associated Press)
Sources: Jensen Huang said Nvidia doesn't need a succession plan because it operates a unique business model and such a plan would create unnecessary hierarchy (CNBC)

item.content:encoded: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after multiple reported affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman who is alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

item.title: Sources: the CIA and the ODNI recently discovered a cybersecurity breach affecting an open-source intelligence analysis system, exposing some unclassified info (New York Times)
President Trump finds himself isolated in DC over his moves to reinstate Jensen Huang as even some of his staunchest allies vow to probe Huang and Nvidia (CNBC)

item.content:encoded: Republicans worry Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affairs with a suspected Chinese spy jeopardized U.S. national security.

item.title: Jensen Huang says he is back not as a "tech bro" or due to Trump's pressure, but because Nvidia's board "evaluated the entire situation" and "gathered facts" (New York Times)
AG Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel dodge reporters' questions about a purported probe that led Trump to push Nvidia's board to bring back Jensen Huang (Dan Mangan/CNBC)

item.content:encoded: The AG and FBI director evaded answering reporters' questions about details of an investigation Trump said resolved security concerns about Jensen Huang.

item.title: Tidal will ban fully AI-generated music starting December 9 and says such content accounted for ~43% of tracks distributed to its platform over the past 90 days (Ethan Millman/The Hollywood Reporter)

item.content:encoded: The service said Tuesday that more than 60 percent of new tracks uploaded to its service on Nov. 6 were fully AI-generated songs.

item.title: In the first all-hands since his return, Jensen Huang apologized for violating Nvidia's code of conduct, saying he made some "very serious personal mistakes" (Paresh Dave/Wired)

item.content:encoded: The Nvidia CEO opened up about his personal life, defended his reinstatement, and acknowledged that his intense management style had hurt his staff.

item.title: Three xAI founding members launch Epochal to build AI agents that achieve "superhuman prediction"; source: co-founder Guodong Zhang personally invested $100M (Bloomberg)

Experts say Trump effectively overrode Nvidia's board, and reinstating Jensen Huang before its probe ends could invite shareholder suits and political scrutiny (New York Times)

AWS CEO Matt Garman says AI safety can't rely on an "emergency brake" and that the same engineering discipline behind decades of secure systems applies to AI (Matt Garman/About Amazon)

Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott says Jensen Huang will testify publicly on December 3, focusing on oversight of US export controls (Emily Birnbaum/Bloomberg)

item.title: Analysis: GTA VI has sold 44.9M copies, not including unsold retail inventory, with the PS5 accounting for 33.7M units, and generated $4B+ in gross revenue (Rhys Elliott/Alinea)
Amazon agrees to acquire much of startup Decart, including the Decart Optimization Stack and its founding team and AI researchers, a source says for ~$7.5B (Matt Day/Bloomberg)
Nvidia's board says it voted to reinstate Jensen Huang after receiving input from "senior levels" of the US government; a probe into his conduct is ongoing (Tim Bradshaw/Financial Times)

President Trump says Nvidia "made the correct and proper decision", the US "needs Jensen's leadership", and the US AG found no evidence of "unlawful conduct" (Donald J. Trump/@realDonaldTrump@truthsocial.com)
Nvidia's board unanimously votes to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, president, and board director effective immediately, after finding no national security risk (Nvidia Newsroom)

item.title: Arm CEO Rene Haas extends his contract through 2033 and will become SoftBank vice chair on December 1; a recruiting firm approached him over becoming Nvidia CEO (Bloomberg)
Marlowe, which develops cloud infrastructure and performance tools to optimize non-Nvidia AI chips, raised a $277M seed led by Accel at a $1.15B valuation (Dina Bass/Bloomberg)
Bret Taylor's customer service AI startup Sierra says it's finalizing a $1.75B+ round led by Lightspeed and Greenoaks at a $30B valuation, up from $15.8B in May (Bloomberg)

Z.ai launches GLM-5.4, a 750B-parameter flagship model built on its Loop Transformer architecture, reaching intelligence levels comparable to 2T-3T models (Z.ai)

A look at AECJ, an Amazon employee group with over 1,000 members that is stepping up efforts to slow Amazon's data center expansion and spark debate over AI use (Rafe Rosner-Uddin/Financial Times)
Boston-based Aevius, whose foundation models analyze patient health using medical records, imaging, and other data, raised a $22M seed led by Insight Partners (Katherine Davis/Axios)
Chinese physical AI startup Simplexity Robotics raised a $100M pre-Series A led by Ant Group, with Alibaba, Tencent, and others joining, at a $1.6B valuation (Saritha Rai/Bloomberg)
Compute Desk, which is building capital markets infrastructure to price, trade, hedge, and clear compute, raised a $45M seed round led by Lightspeed (Lucinda Shen/Axios)
